question: Should OpenClaw adopt this package and generated 15-surface coverage model as the canonical localization foundation before the linked RFC is accepted?
rationale: The patch is technically plausible, but it assigns policy and ownership across core runtime, channels, apps, plugins, CLI, documentation, and security-sensitive copy; that permanent boundary requires maintainer intent rather than automated code judgment.

options.title: Adopt the shared foundation
options.body: Approve the package and coverage contract after localization-owner review, exact-head dependency authorization, and live behavior proof.

options.title: Narrow to current consumers
options.body: Keep only owner-approved Control UI and onboarding fixes while deferring the repository-wide package and coverage contract.

options.title: Wait for RFC acceptance
options.body: Pause the PR until the localization RFC defines the permanent architecture and surface ownership.

recommendation.title: Adopt the shared foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the package and coverage contract after localization-owner review, exact-head dependency authorization, and live behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent public product-direction signal for the repository localization initiative comes from this person.
